problems.name: Running Sum of 1d Array
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, return an array where answer[i] equals nums[0] + nums[1] + ... + nums[i].

examples.explanation: The prefixes are 1, 1+2, 1+2+3, and 1+2+3+4.
Each step adds one more 1 to the previous prefix.
The running total is written at every index.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1) extra if nums is reused as the output.

problems.name: Find Pivot Index
problems.question: Given nums, return the leftmost index where the sum of all elements to the left equals the sum of all elements to the right. Return -1 if no such index exists.

examples.explanation: Left sum 1+7+3 equals right sum 5+6.
No index has equal left and right sums.
At index 0, the left sum is 0 and the right sum is 1 + -1 = 0.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1).

problems.name: Find the Highest Altitude
problems.question: A biker starts at altitude 0. Given gain[i] as the net altitude change between point i and i + 1, return the highest altitude reached.

examples.explanation: Altitudes are 0, -5, -4, 1, 1, -6; the maximum is 1.
Every altitude after the start is below 0, so the highest remains 0.
Altitudes are 0, 2, 4, 1, 0, 2; the maximum is 4.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1).

problems.name: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, choose the minimum positive startValue so that the running sum startValue + nums[0] + ... + nums[i] is always at least 1.

examples.explanation: Prefix sums are -3, -1, -4, 0, 2; lowest is -4, so startValue is 5.
The running sum never drops below 1 when startValue is 1.
Prefix sums are 1, -1, -4; startValue 5 keeps the minimum running sum at 1.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1).

source.label: LeetCode 1413 - Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum

problems.name: Range Sum Query - Immutable
problems.question: Design NumArray so that sumRange(left, right) returns the sum of nums[left] through nums[right] for many immutable range-sum queries.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^4; -10^5 <= nums[i] <= 10^5; 0 <= left <= right < nums.length; at most 10^4 calls to sumRange.

examples.explanation: The full array sum is -3.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Constructor Time O(n), Space O(n); sumRange Time O(1), Space O(1).

problems.name: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
problems.question: Design NumMatrix so that sumRegion(row1, col1, row2, col2) returns the sum of a rectangle in an immutable matrix.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 200; -10^5 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^5; at most 10^4 calls to sumRegion.

examples.explanation: The selected rectangle sums to 8.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Constructor Time O(m*n), Space O(m*n); sumRegion Time O(1), Space O(1).

problems.name: Matrix Block Sum
problems.question: Given a matrix mat and integer k, return answer where answer[i][j] is the sum of all mat[r][c] with |r - i| <= k and |c - j| <= k inside matrix bounds.

examples.explanation: Each answer cell sums its clipped 3x3 neighborhood.
Every block covers the entire matrix.
The only block is the single cell itself.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m*n), Space O(m*n) for prefix and answer.

problems.name: Left and Right Sum Differences
problems.question: Given nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the absolute difference between the sum of elements left of i and the sum of elements right of i.

examples.explanation: At index 1, left sum is 10 and right sum is 11, so the difference is 1.
Both left and right sums are empty and equal to 0.
Each position compares accumulated left sum with remaining right sum.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) for the answer; O(1) extra state.

source.label: LeetCode 2574 - Left and Right Sum Differences

problems.name: Find the Middle Index in Array
problems.question: Given nums, return the leftmost middleIndex where the sum strictly before the index equals the sum strictly after it. Return -1 if none exists.

examples.explanation: Left sum 2+3-1 equals right sum 4.
Left sum 0 equals empty right sum 0.
No index balances the two sides.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1).

source.label: LeetCode 1991 - Find the Middle Index in Array

problems.name: Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays
problems.question: Given an array arr of positive integers, return the sum of all possible odd-length subarrays.

examples.explanation: Odd-length subarray sums are length 1, 3, and 5 totals: 15 + 34 + 9 = 58.
Only odd-length subarrays are [1] and [2].
Single elements sum to 33 and the full length-3 subarray also sums to 33.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2), Space O(n) for prefix sums.

source.label: LeetCode 1588 - Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays

problems.name: Number of Ways to Split Array
problems.question: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, count split positions i where the left part nums[0..i] and right part nums[i+1..n-1] are both non-empty and leftSum >= rightSum.

examples.explanation: Splits after indices 0 and 1 satisfy leftSum >= rightSum.
Splits after indices 1 and 2 are valid.
Only the split after index 1 has left sum -3 >= right sum -3.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(1).

source.label: LeetCode 2270 - Number of Ways to Split Array

problems.name: Maximum Population Year
problems.question: Given birth and death years where a person is alive from birth through death - 1, return the earliest year with the maximum population.

examples.explanation: Population is 1 in 1993 and 2000, so the earliest max year is 1993.
Population reaches 2 first in 1960.
The person is alive in 2000 and not in 2001.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + Y), Space O(Y).

problems.name: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals k.

examples.explanation: The valid subarrays are nums[0..1] and nums[1..2].
The valid subarrays are [1,2] and [3].
Repeated prefix sums count [1,-1], [0], and [1,-1,0].

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) for prefix frequency map.

problems.name: Continuous Subarray Sum
problems.question: Given nums and k, return true if nums has a continuous subarray of length at least 2 whose sum is a multiple of k.

examples.explanation: The subarray [2,4] has sum 6, a multiple of 6.
The subarray [23,2,6,4,7] has sum 42, a multiple of 6.
No length-at-least-2 subarray has sum divisible by 13.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(min(n, k)) for first remainder index map.

problems.name: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
problems.question: Given nums and k, return the number of non-empty subarrays whose sum is divisible by k.

examples.explanation: Seven subarrays have sums divisible by 5.
The only subarray sum is 5, not divisible by 9.
Normalized remainders handle the negative prefix correctly.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(k) for remainder frequencies.

source.label: LeetCode 974 - Subarray Sums Divisible by K

problems.name: Contiguous Array
problems.question: Given a binary array nums, return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0 and 1.

examples.explanation: The full array has one 0 and one 1.
Either [0,1] or [1,0] is balanced.
A longest balanced subarray has equal transformed sum from repeated balance.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) for first balance index map.

problems.name: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
problems.question: Given nums and k, return the maximum length of a subarray that sums to k. Return 0 if no such subarray exists.

examples.explanation: The subarray [1,-1,5,-2] sums to 3 and has length 4.
The subarray [-1,2] sums to 1.
No subarray has sum 7.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n), Space O(n) for first prefix index map.

source.label: LeetCode 325 - Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k

problems.name: Corporate Flight Bookings
problems.question: Given bookings where bookings[i] = [first, last, seats], return seats booked for each flight 1 through n after applying every inclusive range booking.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4; 1 <= bookings.length <= 2 * 10^4; 1 <= first <= last <= n; 1 <= seats <= 10^4.

examples.explanation: Range additions overlap on flights 2 and 3.
Flight 2 receives both bookings.
A single inclusive range updates the only flight.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(b + n), Space O(n) for the difference/result array.

problems.name: Car Pooling
problems.question: Given trips [numPassengers, from, to] and vehicle capacity, return whether all trips can be completed. Passengers are in the car for locations from through to - 1.

examples.explanation: At locations 3 and 4, passenger count becomes 5.
Maximum passenger count is exactly 5.
The first group leaves at 5 before the second group boards from 5.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(t + L), Space O(L), with L <= 1001.

problems.name: Shifting Letters II
problems.question: Given a lowercase string s and shifts [start, end, direction], shift each character in every inclusive range backward for 0 or forward for 1. Return the final string.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length, shifts.length <= 5 * 10^4; shifts[i].length == 3; direction is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: Net shifts are [0,1,2], producing a, c, e.
d shifts backward to c and z shifts forward to a.
The two opposite shifts cancel.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + q), Space O(n) for difference array and output.
